author: William Crooks
title: Eastern Townships sports roundup, Aug. 12: Coaticook beats Granby as cycling and pétanque events approach
text:
Get local news like this every morning. Subscribe free below.
Pulse Newsroom
Eastern Townships teams were active in baseball and soccer Tuesday, Aug. 11, while cycling events in Bromont and Lac-Mégantic and a competitive pétanque tournament in Granby are coming up later this week.
In junior-elite baseball, Rocket South Shore de Coaticook defeated the Guerriers de Granby 17-11.
Results posted through Spordle show Coaticook at 23-22 in the latest standings, with Granby at 22-22.
At 15U B, Val-des-Sources Diamond played Victoriaville’s Laurier to a 9-9 draw, while Granby’s Phénix beat the Waterloo Vikings 14-9 in western 13U A play.
A late-posted Monday result also showed Sherbrooke’s White Sox edging Val-des-Sources Diamond 6-5 at 13U B. The latest standings had the clubs tied at 18 points, with Sherbrooke third and Val-des-Sources fourth.
Rainbow remains unbeaten in Sherbrooke soccer
Soccer results posted through Spordle show Rainbow shut out CF Sherbrooke 7-0 in an all-Sherbrooke Senior Regional Female D1 game.
The latest standings listed Rainbow at 14-0 with 42 points, while CF Sherbrooke was second with 26.
In Senior Regional Male D3-2, the Avengers of Haut-Saint-François edged Magog 4-3 in a meeting of the top two teams in the latest standings.
Haut-Saint-François was first with 33 points, three ahead of Magog. Windsor also defeated Sherbrooke Légende FC 6-0 and had 30 points despite having played two fewer games than Haut-Saint-François.
In the Cantons league, the Farnham Invincibles beat CS de Cowansville 4-3 at U17 Local Mixed.
Late-posted Monday results included a 0-0 draw between Celtic Richmond and Haut-Saint-François LL-2 at U16 Local Female. Richmond led the latest standings with 28 points, five ahead of HSF LL-2.
At U14 Local Female, HSF LL-2 defeated Celtic Richmond 3-1, while HSF LL-1 and Coaticook’s Eclipse drew 1-1. Lac-Brome Thunder also beat Aigles d’Or 2-1 in Cantons league play.
BMX freestyle begins in Bromont Thursday
The Bromont National Cycling Centre is preparing for the 2026 Canadian BMX Freestyle Championships on Friday, Aug. 14.
According to the centre, unofficial open practice will run Thursday from 4 to 8 p.m.
Friday’s program has the gates opening at 8 a.m., followed by licence verification and official practice sessions for elite and open competitors.
The event is scheduled to open to the public at 5:30 p.m., with Elite and Open competition from 6 to 9 p.m. and awards at 9 p.m.
The centre says elite and amateur riders from across Canada will compete in the CNCB Freestyle Zone.
The centre notes that Cycling Canada’s technical guide takes precedence over the schedule posted on its website.
Three cycling events in Lac-Mégantic
The City of Lac-Mégantic says its Grande journée du vélo will take place Saturday, Aug. 15, from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.
The day combines three events: the Grand Tour du lac, Gran Fondo and Grand Gravel Bike Lac-Mégantic.
According to the city, the events will start consecutively from the Centre sportif Mégantic on different routes, with participants returning to Parc des Vétérans.
The city also says activities will be held on site throughout the day.
Competitive pétanque in Granby
The City of Granby lists the Tournoi de pétanque Boustifailles for Saturday and Sunday, Aug. 15-16.
The city describes it as a competitive pétanque tournament and méchoui that is open to the public.
Registration information is being provided through the organizers, with additional event details available through Granby Multi-Sports.
